claim: COMCL5 expansion: NEWCL5 hard-codes the CLIFF5 start X pixel as $1B*2 = 54 — one of the two independent source statements that corroborate the expanded island's origin (the other is CLIF5's own dest word $1BD3).

source.verbatim: NEWCL5	LDX	#$1B*2		START X PIXEL POSITION ON SCREEN

claim: COMCL5 expansion: NEWCL5 hard-codes the start Y pixel as $D3 = 211, the scanline the bottom island begins on.

source.verbatim: LDY	#$D3		START Y PIXEL POSITION ON SCREEN

claim: COMCL5 stream format: the run-length codeword opens with a UNARY prefix — INCA counts one more encoded length per bit until a 1 bit is found (UNCLP). This is what makes the stream Elias-gamma coded rather than the value/run byte pairs a first reading suggests.

source.verbatim: 10$	INCA			1 MORE ENCODED LENGTH

claim: COMCL5 stream format: the decoded gamma codeword is TWO more than the run length — "CODEWORD & RUN LENGTH ARE TWO OFF". A decoder that skipped this subtraction over-draws every run by two pixels.

source.verbatim: SUBA	#2		CODEWORD & RUN LENGTH ARE TWO OFF

claim: COMCL5 stream format: exactly three further bits carry the colour code, read by the same REST routine as the run length.

source.verbatim: LDA	#3		GET 3 BIT COLOR ??NIBBLE??

claim: COMCL5 stream format: a run length of zero means end-of-line, or end-of-image when the three colour bits are also zero — the two terminators are distinguished only by the colour field.

source.verbatim: ANDA	#$07		"END OF LINE" OR "END OF IMAGE"?

claim: COMCL5 colour mapping: ADDA #8-1 maps colour codes 1..7 onto palette nibbles 8..14, while code 0 stays nibble 0. This is why the expansion can only ever emit the alphabet {0} u {8..14} — a decoder omitting this step emits 1..7 and produces a plausible image in entirely the wrong colours.

source.verbatim: ADDA	#8-1

claim: COMCL5 stream format: REST seeds the accumulator with an implicit leading 1 before shifting in the fetched bits — the Elias-gamma reconstruction step.

source.verbatim: LDA	#1		RUN LENGTH START BIT

claim: COMCL5 expansion: on end-of-line the destination advances exactly one scanline (LEAY 1,Y) and X reloads to the start of the line, which is what makes the expanded island rows ragged rather than a padded rectangle.

source.verbatim: LEAY	1,Y		NEXT PIXEL LINE

claim: ASH1R/ASH1L format, stated by the author: the pterodactyl-dissolve stream is one byte per run — LOW nibble is the colour, HIGH nibble is the length. This closes open-questions §5, which recorded the format as undecoded.

source.verbatim: 2$	LDA	,Y+	lo nybble is color, hi nybble is length

claim: ASH1R/ASH1L format: a byte of $00 (length and colour both zero) terminates the image.

source.verbatim: BEQ	1$	length & color equ 0, end of image

claim: ASH1R/ASH1L format: the colour nibble is replicated into both halves of the byte by multiplying by 17 ($0A -> $AA), so a run writes whole BYTES — two pixels at a time — not single pixels.

source.verbatim: LDB	#17	replicate lo nybble ($0A-=-$AA) for color

claim: ASH1R/ASH1L format: a length nibble of zero means end-of-line; the destination then advances one scanline.

source.verbatim: BNE	3$	if length equ 0, end of line

claim: ASH1R/ASH1L format: the LAST byte of every run is masked to its high nibble alone, so each run ends on a single pixel rather than a full byte — "last byte is always one pixel to enhance debris image". This is why run lengths counted as pixels give ragged, inconsistent row widths.

source.verbatim: CMPA	#1	last byte is always one pixel to enhance debris image

claim: ASH1R/ASH1L format: the destination advances by $100 per byte because Williams images are stored column-major — the blitter walks down a column, not across a row.

source.verbatim: LEAX	$100,X	next location is over 1 as our images are horizontally

claim: ASH1R/ASH1L consumer: the pterodactyl death path loads ASH1R into its frame pointer, the trace that identifies which game state consumes the dissolve stream.

source.verbatim: LDD	ASH1R		PTERODACTYL ASHES TO ASHES

claim: Transcription hazard: CCLF1L's collision mask opens here, and its comment runs off the end of the line without a continuation marker.

source.verbatim: CCLF1L	FDB	10+COFF,35+32+COFF	CLIF1L STARTS -9 TO 33 PIXEL (INCLUDING

claim: Transcription hazard: the tail of the previous line's comment sits alone in the LABEL column, indistinguishable by shape from a real label. A transcription honouring it truncates CCLF1L's 8-row mask to ONE row and attributes the other seven to an invented symbol — a wrong collision mask that is still well-formed, so nothing downstream complains.

source.verbatim: ZERO)

claim: Transcription hazard: the second comment-wrap case, whose tail lands on the following line.

source.verbatim: CCLF1R	FDB	1+COFF,36+32+COFF		CLIF1R GOES 10 MORE PIXELS OFF S

claim: Transcription hazard: CREEN is comment-wrap debris in the label column, but unlike ZERO) it is a well-formed uppercase identifier, so NO shape heuristic can separate it from a real label. The discriminator that works is semantic: a real label is referenced somewhere in the file, comment debris is referenced by nothing.

source.verbatim: CREEN

claim: CLIFF5 sub-record: the left-side cap CSRC5L is drawn as 8 bytes by 13 scanlines ($080D pre-XORed with DMAFIX), but the CSRC5L data below holds FOURTEEN rows of 8. The record draws 13 of the 14 available rows; the transcription keeps all 112 bytes rather than truncating to the record.

source.verbatim: FDB	      CSRC5L,$1BD3,$080D!XDMAFIX	LEFT SIDE

claim: CLIFF5 sub-record: this is the fourteenth and final row of CSRC5L data — the row CLIF5s 13-scanline sub-record never draws.
Palette: the NULL palette of sixteen zero entries begins here, immediately after HICOLR's eight live entries — which is why the high-score page palette reads as 8 live colours followed by 8 black.

source.verbatim: NULL	FCB	@000

claim: Image module extent: LENGTH EQU * marks the end of the merged images module, the running total the transcription must reach to prove no trailing block was dropped.

source.verbatim: LENGTH	EQU	*	CURRENT TOTAL LENGTH OF IMAGES
